subject: Structuring pilot discounts for cache-first workloads
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgecast.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing for cache-heavy inference (EdgeCast)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our ML infra team is excited about Redwood’s cache-first recommendations for our streaming summarization endpoint. Before we lock a pilot, procurement has asked for a short commercial proposal that explains:
- Suggested pilot credit structure (how credits apply to cached vs non-cached tokens)
- Any quantization/accuracy caveats if we move to lower precision for production
- A simple example of expected token spend with prefix reuse (~70% prefix hit)

Can you send a one-pager or example quote we can share internally? Procurement (cc’d) needs something by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Maria
Director of ML Engineering, EdgeCast AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgecast.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing for cache-heavy inference (EdgeCast)

Hi Maria —

Appreciate the clear asks. I put together a compact commercial sketch below; attaching a short pricing grid & a draft SOW that maps credits to pilot deliverables. High level:

1) Pilot credit split (recommended):
   - 4 weeks, capped: 600k effective tokens
   - 65% credited to prefix/KV-hit tokens (cache-first rate)
   - Remaining 35% billed at hosted pay-as-you-go rates (for cold starts / experiments)

2) How credits apply:
   - We tag tokens as KV-hit vs KV-miss at runtime. Credits consume KV-hit-first buckets; only KV-miss tokens draw from the billed pool. This prevents you from being charged for steady-state streaming traffic that benefits from prefix reuse.

3) Quantization guidance:
   - For latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend int8 per-channel quant with layerwise calibration for your T5-style models. In our tests this gives ~2.4x throughput at ~<1.5% delta on Rouge/Ling evals. If you want aggressive compression (mixed int4), we can include a conservative quality SLA carveout in the SOW.

4) Example spend (70% prefix reuse, 80k incoming prompts/day over 30 days):
   - Gross tokens: ~2.4M tokens
   - KV-hit tokens: ~1.68M (credited)
   - KV-miss tokens billed: ~720k -> expected billed token spend equivalent: ~$3.8k for the month (pilot rates)

Next steps: I’ve attached a table that codifies the split and a draft SOW. Kimberly — can we lock the concession bands for a 4-week pilot and confirm whether legal needs a different SOW template?

Thanks — rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot pricing for cache-heavy inference (EdgeCast)

Maria — quick note from the commercial side:

- We can do the 65/35 split Rishi suggested. For a first pilot we typically layer a small one-time onboarding credit (10% of pilot size) to cover integration effort.
- If you want an option to extend to Dedicated capacity after the pilot, we can include a rollover credit equal to unused pilot credits (valid for 90 days) if you sign a 12‑month reserved capacity commit within 30 days of pilot close.

Ben — please validate the quantization SLA language and confirm any ops guardrails (burst vs slab) we should call out.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@edgecast.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing for cache-heavy inference (EdgeCast)

Thanks — technical/commercial notes from my side:

Operational guardrails (recommended for the SOW):
- Prefix hit target: we set an initial target of >=60% KV-hit for steady-state; we’ll instrument with live KV-hit metrics in the Console and run a one-week tuning window during the pilot.
- Burst handling: allow up to 2x burst capacity for short windows (first 30s of traffic spike) billed as burst tokens, not charging against KV-hit credits. This prevents routing friction for your spike tests.

Quantization specifics (what to include in SOW):
- Default: int8 per-channel quant with layerwise calibration. We’ll run an eval suite on your dev prompts. If accuracy drop <=1.5% on chosen metrics -> apply production int8 path.
- Optional: mixed-int4 trial under a canary flag with manual rollback; include a quality regression clause that triggers a revert if delta >3%.

Pricing math note (we used Rishi’s numbers):
- Pilot effective cost to EdgeCast (after credits & onboarding): ~USD 1,800 net for 4 weeks (reflects pilot discount, onboarding credit, and expected prefix reuse).

Attachments: I uploaded a short pricing grid (optimize_pricing_grid.xlsx) and a draft SOW (SOW_edgecast_draft.pdf) that breaks out the credit accounting logic.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
